title: Penguins Chase 13 Goals in Two Wins: DK Pittsburgh Sports Highlights Stunning Scoring Surge
body:
PITTSBURGH – The Pittsburgh Penguins turned a dramatic near‑collapse into a thrilling overtime victory on opening night, edging the Montreal Canadiens 6‑5 after surrendering a four‑goal lead in the third period. A decisive one‑timer from rookie forward Tommy Novak in the extra frame capped a roller‑coaster performance that highlighted both the team’s offensive firepower and lingering defensive lapses.

The early stages of the game seemed to belong to Pittsburgh. A flurry of goals in the first two periods—highlighted by a power‑play conversion from veteran center Jake Guentzel and a crisp backhand from winger Evgeni Malkin—propelled the Penguins to a comfortable 4‑0 advantage. Coach Mike Sullivan appeared to have the squad settled, rotating lines efficiently and maintaining puck possession in the offensive zone. The crowd at PPG Paints Arena was already buzzing, confident that the season’s first home game would set a positive tone.

Montreal, however, refused to capitulate. After a disciplined penalty kill, the Canadiens sparked a resurgence with a quick two‑goal burst midway through the third, narrowing the gap to 4‑2. The momentum shift was palpable; the Canadiens pressed aggressively, forcing turnovers and capitalizing on a misplayed breakout by Pittsburgh’s third line. A power‑play goal by forward Nick Suzuki tied the game at 4‑4, and a subsequent even‑strength strike from Jonathan Drouin gave Montreal a 5‑4 lead with just under five minutes remaining. The sudden reversal left the Penguins scrambling, and a late‑period goal from Canadiens defenseman Jeff Petry extended the lead to 6‑4, seemingly sealing the upset.

Pittsburgh’s response was swift and emblematic of their resilience. Forward Jonathan Sparks ignited the comeback with a gritty goal that cut the deficit to one, followed by a perfectly timed pass to rookie Tommy Novak, whose blistering one‑timer found the back of the net to knot the game at 6‑6. The arena erupted as the overtime horn sounded, and the Penguins seized the moment. Novak, riding the momentum of his equalizer, collected the puck in the neutral zone, faked a defender, and unleashed a powerful shot from the left circle that beat Canadiens goaltender Jake Allen high on the glove side, clinching the win.

The win, while exhilarating, underscores a recurring theme for the Penguins: explosive offense coupled with defensive vulnerability. Over the first two games of the season, Pittsburgh has tallied an impressive 13 goals, averaging 6.5 per contest, yet has also allowed nine. Defensive coordinator Dave Gordon will likely face scrutiny as the coaching staff evaluates zone coverage and transition breakdowns that allowed Montreal to claw back from a sizable lead. Goaltender Tristan Jarry posted a respectable 33‑save performance, but the high volume of high‑danger chances against suggests that tighter defensive structures will be essential if the Penguins hope to sustain early‑season momentum.

Looking ahead, the Penguins return to the ice this weekend against the New York Rangers, a matchup that will test whether the team can translate its offensive prowess into more disciplined play. If Sullivan can tighten the back end while maintaining the scoring depth that produced 13 goals in two games, Pittsburgh could solidify its status as a contender in the Eastern Conference. For now, the overtime triumph over Montreal provides a confidence boost and a reminder that, despite occasional lapses, the Penguins possess the firepower to rebound from adversity and compete at the highest level.
